articles.title: Connect AUX-2 brings older equipment into the smart home
articles.dek: Nabu Casa launches a $69 / €59 box for audio, serial control, Bluetooth and network-connected Z-Wave, with power over Ethernet.
body: Nabu Casa launches Home Assistant Connect AUX-2 worldwide for $69 / €59. The small box connects existing audio equipment, compatible serial devices and Bluetooth devices to the open home. One Ethernet cable can supply both its network connection and power; USB power and Wi-Fi are alternatives.

For an older hi-fi, AUX-2 supplies analog or optical digital audio through Music Assistant and Sendspin. A compatible amplifier’s serial connection can also control its volume, source and power. Two serial ports connect equipment such as televisions and climate systems, provided Home Assistant supports the device and the right cable is used.

AUX-2 also acts as a Bluetooth proxy and lets a USB-connected Z-Wave adapter sit somewhere with better coverage than the Home Assistant computer. In the launch post, Nabu Casa product manager Shay Redmond recommends a wired connection. Zigbee-over-network support is still being tested, and Thread is not supported over this connection.

The hardware is unlocked for custom firmware, and a Grove port accepts additional sensors with an ESPHome configuration. Four screws provide access to the inside; Nabu Casa says it will also publish the circuit-board and 3D-print files.

articles.title: Copy a whole Home Assistant dashboard without editing configuration
articles.dek: A duplicate includes every view and redirects its internal links to the new copy.
body: Home Assistant adds Duplicate to the menu for user-created dashboards in Settings. The new-dashboard dialog lets someone choose a name and settings before copying every view, replacing the manual configuration copying that was particularly awkward on a phone.

Internal navigation that points to the original dashboard is redirected to the copy when its link starts at the site’s root. Links retain their destination views and other details. Require admin and Show in sidebar are chosen in the dialog rather than copied from the original.

Point links in a duplicated dashboard at the copy

articles.title: EZVIZ cameras connect without turning off two-step verification
articles.dek: Home Assistant asks for the verification code instead of requiring weaker account protection.
body: Home Assistant lets an EZVIZ account complete setup with two-step verification still enabled. Previously, a request for a code stopped setup and told the owner to disable that protection in the EZVIZ app.

The setup flow requests the code and completes the same sign-in session when it is entered. The prompt also covers signing in again and changing an existing connection; a wrong or expired code produces an error. The contributor verified setup with a real account and its cameras.

pullRequests.title: Add verification code step to EZVIZ config flow

articles.title: Home Assistant reaches camera talkback sooner
articles.dek: The camera viewer spends less time waiting for the connection that supports two-way audio.
body: Home Assistant shortens the wait for the WebRTC connection used by camera talkback. Cameras could spend ten to twenty-five seconds on an alternative video stream, or remain there without two-way audio becoming available.

The browser tries fewer redundant relay addresses and remembers cameras where WebRTC previously worked, trying that connection first on later visits. Failed connections receive up to two retries, carrying an active microphone into the replacement connection.
On three cameras in Chrome, Wendelin measured the first opening falling from twelve to twenty-six seconds to six to nine seconds. Those timings apply to that installation.

pullRequests.title: Make camera WebRTC streams connect faster and more reliably

articles.title: Danish radio and podcasts join Music Assistant
articles.dek: A community-built DR LYD connection brings live stations, programme browsing and podcast search into one player.
body: Music Assistant adds a connection to DR LYD, the audio service of Danish public broadcaster DR. Listeners can browse its live radio channels, search podcasts, and find programmes alphabetically or by their latest episode.

The provider is marked beta and community-maintained. It reads the same radio service used by the DR LYD website and updates the playing station’s programme and track information. Mikkel Eskildsen makes his first contribution to Music Assistant’s server with the integration.

pullRequests.title: Add DR LYD provider

articles.title: ESPHome retrieves lost configuration files from the device
articles.dek: A built-in recovery command turns an embedded backup into a folder ready to repair and reuse.
body: ESPHome adds a recovery command that downloads a device’s saved configuration and writes it to a new folder. It retrieves the main YAML file and its included files, keeping their relative paths, without requiring the lost original configuration to connect.

This gives makers a built-in way to retrieve the device-held backups reported on November 5. The device must already have configuration storage enabled, and an encrypted device requires its API key. Recognized secrets normally return as placeholders to fill in; the command refuses to overwrite a nonempty destination folder.

pullRequests.title: [store_yaml] Add esphome recover-yaml to download the stored YAML

articles.title: Home Assistant exposes hidden list actions to screen readers
articles.dek: Zone-edit buttons and integration-device menus become separate accessible controls.
body: Home Assistant makes action buttons inside settings list rows visible to screen readers. Controls such as the edit button beside a zone and the menu beside an integration device were nested inside the row’s own button, leaving assistive software unable to expose them.
Those controls stand separately from the row’s main link or button. The full row remains clickable, while keyboard shortcuts and touch exploration keep working.

pullRequests.title: Expose action buttons in list rows to screen readers

articles.title: Music Assistant follows your latest podcast or audiobook position
articles.dek: A newer rewind or reset in another app can take precedence over the furthest point played.
body: Music Assistant uses one rule to reconcile its saved listening position with a podcast or audiobook provider’s progress. Where the provider supplies an update time, the newer position wins—including a deliberate rewind or reset made in another app. Without that timestamp, the furthest position still wins.

Fabian Munkes applies the rule across playback, episode pages and library updates, using timestamps from sources including Audiobookshelf, gPodder and Overcast. Eric Munson also corrects Subsonic bookmarks to use their last modification time. An episode listing can still miss progress for a user who is behind when several users share a provider without an owner.

articles.title: Choose how much reasoning an OpenRouter voice agent uses
articles.dek: Supported models can use less reasoning to reduce the wait for an answer.
body: Home Assistant adds a Reasoning option for OpenRouter conversation agents, with model-supported choices including automatic, on, off and effort levels. Reducing the effort offers a way to shorten the wait for a voice answer.
The setup rejects choices the selected model cannot support, including Off when reasoning is mandatory. Existing agents retain their behavior, and the setting does not change AI tasks.

articles.dek: Owners may need to enable Sync to China in the Home Connect developer portal.
body: Home Assistant uses Home Connect’s China service when the installation’s configured country is China, as required by Home Connect for applications there. Other installations keep the global service. Affected owners may need to enable Sync to China in the Home Connect developer portal; setup links also lead to the China portal.

articles.title: ESPHome keeps brief Zigbee radio loss from risking a factory reset
articles.dek: End devices wait for repeated failures before leaving and rejoining their network.
body: ESPHome stops a single missed Zigbee exchange from forcing an end device to leave and rejoin its network. Those unnecessary rejoins could end in a factory reset, particularly while Bluetooth scanning shared the radio.

The device waits for four failed polls spanning at least six seconds. In an ESP32-C6 test, 21 isolated failures caused no rejoin, while a missing coordinator still triggered one after nine seconds. A genuine rejoin can still hit the underlying reset problem.

pullRequests.title: [zigbee] Rejoin only after the parent missed several polls

articles.title: Home Assistant lets idle Acaia scales switch themselves off
articles.dek: An optional timeout releases the Bluetooth connection that otherwise prevents the scale’s own auto-off timer.
body: Home Assistant adds an optional idle timeout for Acaia scales so they can use their own automatic power-off and conserve their battery. The integration previously kept Bluetooth connected around the clock, preventing the scale from sleeping.

The owner chooses how long an unchanged weight counts as idle; the option starts disabled. After disconnecting, Home Assistant waits for the scale to power off and return before reconnecting. The sequence was tested on a Lunar.

pullRequests.title: Add idle disconnect timeout option to acaia

articles.title: Music Assistant keeps quiet tracks from distorting when boosted
articles.dek: Automatic limiting catches peaks when volume normalization turns a track up.
body: Music Assistant catches peaks that would distort when volume normalization turns a quiet track up. Previously, listeners needed to add their own safety limiter to prevent that clipping. Tracks that are turned down are unchanged. When the player and every grouped speaker handle audio processing themselves, their settings remain responsible for limiting.

pullRequests.title: Prevent clipping when volume normalization raises a quiet track

articles.title: ESPHome adjusts CO₂ sensors to a chosen reference
articles.dek: Two Sensirion families gain controls for correcting readings against a known concentration.
body: ESPHome gives makers control over the reference used by two Sensirion CO₂ sensor families. Compatible SCD4x firmware can use a chosen automatic-calibration target instead of the fixed 400 ppm baseline; older firmware keeps the default.

SEN63C, SEN66 and SEN69C sensors gain a separate action to recalibrate against a reference concentration. Measurements must be stopped during that operation. The target-setting check used an SCD40, while forced recalibration was tested on a SEN66.

articles.title: Reolink recordings play again after recorder firmware changes
articles.dek: Home Assistant changes the playback path for network recorders and hubs; Safari remains outside the fix.
body: Home Assistant restores playback of Reolink recorder footage affected by recent firmware changes. It uses Reolink’s recording protocol for network video recorders and hubs, converting the video for browser playback. Safari on iOS still needs separate support for its partial-file requests.

pullRequests.title: Fix Reolink playback for NVRs and Hubs

articles.title: Matter.js shortens a blind spot in door-lock updates
articles.dek: Controllers using the library replace some failed state subscriptions sooner.
body: Matter.js recovers sooner when a device stops sending state changes after a report goes unanswered. A Thread door lock in the supporting log left its controller with stale readings for about five minutes, even while requests from the controller still worked.

For subscriptions that can resume with a compact update, the library starts recovery once delivery retries fail—about a minute in that Thread case. Subscriptions requiring a full initial report retain the longer timeout.

pullRequests.title: fix(protocol): replace a subscription when the peer does not ack our report status

articles.title: Music Assistant removes its built-in Auracast connection
articles.dek: The experimental broadcast provider is being moved to a separate app to keep hardware dependencies out of the server.
body: Music Assistant removes the experimental Auracast connection covered on November 4. The project is moving it to a separate app so the Bluetooth-broadcasting hardware dependencies can stay outside the server. The removed connection sent audio to compatible Bluetooth LE Audio receivers through a supported controller.

pullRequests.title: Remove Auracast

articles.title: An Android phone’s volume buttons can control a remote speaker
articles.dek: An optional setting sends button presses to the selected Music Assistant player while the app is in focus.
body: Music Assistant’s Android app lets a phone’s physical volume buttons control the selected remote speaker. The optional setting applies while the app has focus, with an overlay showing the speaker’s volume. Andrii Mitnovych’s addition uses the same step commands as the on-screen controls; Android’s media-session behavior outside the app stays unchanged.

pullRequests.title: Let the volume keys control the remote player on Android (opt-in)

articles.title: Sonoff’s temperature display adds a second remote source
articles.dek: The firmware update requires existing remote temperature and humidity sources to be configured again.
body: Firmware 1.0.5 for the Sonoff SNZB-02DR2 adds support for two remote temperature and humidity sources. Jiyon Yu submits the update to Zigpy’s firmware collection, with testing recorded on the device. Owners must configure any existing remote sources again after updating.

roadmapUpdates.summary: While Home Assistant shapes its proposed weather page, Laura asks whether weather conditions and their effects on heating and energy belong in separate views or together. That design question remains open; the opportunity stays in Shaping.
